findings.where: Title-block nav bar, desktop and phone: the DRAWING MMM-GA-001 and SCALE NTS cells beside PROFILE / ARTICLES / BLOG / CONTACT
findings.fault: The drawing number and scale sit in the same ruled cells as the four menu links, with the same spaced capitals in the same colour. Because they look alike and share one region, they read as two more menu items, but they do nothing. On the phone it is worse: they share the top row with the logo, and the real links drop to a second row, so the bar looks like eight equal cells.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development bank looking for Mark's profile or contact, who clicks 'MMM-GA-001' expecting a page and gets nothing, or has to work out which cells are the menu.

findings.where: Hero on the phone (phone-01, first screen): the drawing, the name, the paragraph and the Write to Mark button
findings.fault: On the desktop the section drawing fills the sheet and the words wait below it. On the phone the drawing shrinks to a strip about 150 px tall, and the name, the two caption lines, the paragraph and the button take the rest of the first screen. Text wins the squint, so 'the picture leads and the words wait' is lost at this width.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose 'calm first' value asks for one quiet picture before any text asks for anything. A visitor on a phone gets a page of text with a small diagram above it.

findings.where: Texture specimen on the phone (phone-01, bottom): the EARTH HATCH and POCHE boxes inside their frame
findings.fault: The specimen breaks at this width. The hatch box and its label are pushed flush against the frame's left edge, and the poche box runs into the right edge, with no inner margin on either side. The dimension line that spans the boxes on the desktop is gone, which leaves an empty ruled strip under them. It reads as a broken component, not a drawn detail.
findings.who_objects: Mark and the layout round reviewing the tile on a phone. The one part meant to show the drawing's texture looks unfinished, which undercuts a direction whose whole idea is precision.

findings.where: Hero caption under MARK M. MOSELEY: 'INFRASTRUCTURE ADVISOR / LONGITUDINAL SECTION A-A · SCALE NTS'
findings.fault: Mark's actual role is stacked tight against the drawing's section and scale notes, in the same size, tracking and colour. By proximity and similarity it reads as one more line of drawing metadata, not as who he is.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor scanning to learn what Mark does. 'Infrastructure advisor' is the one line that answers it, and it is treated as a caption on the drawing.

findings.where: Bottom of the desktop sheet (desktop-03): the article specimen column beside the motion-sketch panel
findings.fault: The article column ends about 220 px above the motion panel, which leaves an empty block at the lower left before the sheet border. The two columns end out of balance, and the sheet's lower edge feels unfinished.
findings.who_objects: A designer or Mark reviewing the tile. The rest of the sheet is laid out with drawing-office care, so the ragged finish stands out. Few others would notice.

findings.where: Motion-sketch timeline table on the phone (phone-02/03)
findings.fault: The four columns keep their desktop split, so the ELEMENT column is squeezed to two or three words a line. Each row wraps over three lines, while the number columns sit in wide, mostly empty space.
findings.who_objects: The animation round reading the timeline on a phone, who has to piece each element's name back together across line breaks.
